candidate_relations.reason: Neonatal hypotonia, stridor, corneal opacity, congenital cardiac anomalies, and an ATAD3A p.Q506P variant do not describe Hutchinson-Gilford progeria.
The infant has upper-airway stridor and swollen aryepiglottic folds rather than documented sleep-related hypoventilation or a PHOX2B variant.
There is no generalized lymphangiectasia, lymphedema, or intestinal protein loss to support Hennekam syndrome, while testing identifies an ATAD3A variant.
The record reports a specific heterozygous ATAD3A variant and lacks the clenched hands, growth restriction, and chromosomal result required for trisomy 18.
Neither a trisomy-21 karyotype nor its characteristic phenotype is reported, whereas the multisystem neonatal disorder is linked to ATAD3A c.1517A>C.
A small lower jaw alone does not establish Pierre Robin syndrome because glossoptosis and cleft palate are not reported and do not explain the ocular, neurologic, and cardiac findings.
Neck and laryngeal CT was normal and bronchoscopy showed swollen aryepiglottic folds, while laryngomalacia would not account for hypotonia, corneal opacity, and congenital heart anomalies.
No trisomy-13 test or typical midline malformation is documented, and genetic testing instead found an ATAD3A p.Q506P variant.
Flaccid limbs and neonatal hypotonia are prominent features of the ATAD3A-related syndrome but do not identify its genetic multisystem cause.
Low oxygen saturation occurred with stridor, pneumonia, and upper-airway swelling, without evidence of central hypoventilation or a PHOX2B mutation.
The combination of corneal opacity, hypotonia, congenital cardiac defects, and an ATAD3A variant supports Harel-Yoon syndrome rather than Helsinki syndrome.
Generalized hypotonia is documented from birth, but it is one neurologic feature and does not encompass the ATAD3A-associated ocular, airway, facial, and cardiac disease.
A neonate with choking and excessive secretions has no endoscopic evidence of intestinalized distal esophageal mucosa or chronic reflux required for Barrett esophagus.
Although micrognathia developed, the absence of glossoptosis and cleft palate and the presence of corneal opacity and ATAD3A-associated hypotonia argue against Pierre Robin sequence.
The heterozygous ATAD3A c.1517A>C p.Q506P finding supports a heterozygous ATAD3A-related disorder, but the label omits the clinically specified Harel-Yoon syndrome phenotype.
Birth weight at nearly 38 weeks was 2790 g and no profound growth failure or microcephaly is described, making MOPD type I incompatible with this presentation.
ATAD3A-related disorder correctly captures the implicated gene but does not specify the Harel-Yoon syndrome subtype represented by the neonatal multisystem findings.
The record lacks cerebellar hypoplasia, immunodeficiency, marrow failure, and a telomere-gene defect characteristic of Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome.
A neonatal ATAD3A phenotype with congenital anomalies is unlike MNGIE, which requires gastrointestinal dysmotility, ophthalmoplegia, leukoencephalopathy, and TYMP-related evidence.
No contractures, pulmonary hypoplasia, or fetal akinesia sequence is reported, while the infant's ocular and cardiac anomalies accompany an ATAD3A variant.
